checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Final video retains original coworkers, setting, sequence, 10-second duration
must.why: No final video was produced. The agent supplied only a WAV and told the user to lay it over the clip in an editor. The footage is untouched, but nothing was combined.

must.item: Intelligible English narrator explains coworkers discussing schedule change and Monday start at nine
must.why: The script text says this, but I only have voice-preview images and sounds. The final WAV was not checked.

must.item: Narration does not invent names, roles, or extra schedule changes
must.why: The script only mentions two coworkers, the new schedule, and Mondays at nine. All of it came from the user.

must.item: Original man-and-woman conversation no longer audible beneath narration
must.why: No mixed output exists. The user must mute the original audio manually.

must.item: Narration fits within video without clipped ending; no music or captions added
must.why: The claimed 6–8 s length was not checked. No music or captions were added to the footage because the footage was not touched.

faults.what: No finished video was delivered. The user must mute the original audio and add the narration in an editor, so the audio-replacement request is only partly met.
The script says 'two coworkers', but the frame shows three people: two men and a woman seen from behind. This is a small mismatch, and the user supplied the description.
The narration length of 6–8 s was claimed but not checked. The images and sounds I have are only voice-sample previews.

summary: The agent wrote a short, accurate script and made a narration WAV, but it delivered no final video, so the user must replace the audio manually. I could not check the WAV or its timing.
